rules.title: Oakland Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance - Owner/Relative Move-In and Related Grounds
rules.requirement: Landlords may only evict tenants for specific listed causes such as owner move-in, substantial repairs, or Ellis Act withdrawal, and must follow strict notice, timing, and tenant-protection rules, including special protections for long-term elderly, disabled, or catastrophically ill tenants and families with school-age children.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental units covered by Oakland's Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (O.M.C. Chapter 8.22, Article II), subject to exemptions in Section 8.22.350.
rules.exemptions: Units exempt under Section 8.22.350 of the Chapter; certain protections do not apply where qualifying relative is 60+, disabled, or catastrophically ill and all other units owned by landlord are occupied by protected tenants.
rules.penalty: Failure to comply with notice, filing, or procedural requirements is a defense to any unlawful detainer action; landlord bears burden of proof; tenant may recover reasonable expenses including lease termination fees if owner/relative move-in requirement is violated.
rules.quoted_span: The owner of record seeks in good faith, without ulterior reasons and with honest intent, to recover possession for their own use and occupancy as their principal residence, or for the use and occupancy as a principal residence by the owner of record's spouse, domestic partner, child, parent, or grandparent.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the unit is exempt under Section 8.22.350 of the Chapter (not detailed in this chunk)

rules.title: Oakland Just Cause Eviction - Substantial Repairs Ground
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict a tenant to complete substantial repairs needed to bring a unit into code compliance, but must offer the tenant first right of return at the same rent and terms after repairs are completed, and the tenant's displacement generally may not exceed three months absent Rent Board extension.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental units covered by the Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance where landlord seeks possession for substantial repairs under Subsection 8.22.360 A.10.
rules.penalty: Failure to comply with relocation payment or notice requirements is a defense to any action for possession of a rental unit.
rules.quoted_span: Upon completion of the needed repairs, the owner of record shall offer the tenant the first right to return to the premises at the same rent and pursuant to the same terms of the rental agreement in effect as of the date of the notice to vacate, subject to the owner of record's right to petition the Rent Adjustment Program for a rent increase as provided by the Residential Rent Adjustment Ordinance.

rules.title: Oakland Just Cause Eviction - COVID-19 Nonpayment Defense
rules.requirement: In eviction cases based on nonpayment of rent or late fees that accrued between March 9, 2020 and July 14, 2023, tenants have a defense if the nonpayment resulted from substantial pandemic-related loss of income or increased expenses, and landlords must include a specific notice statement informing tenants of this defense.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to unlawful detainer actions based on nonpayment of rent or late fees accrued between March 9, 2020 and July 14, 2023.
rules.penalty: Failure to serve required hardship-defense form and statement undermines the notice; noncompliance can be raised as a defense in eviction proceedings.
rules.quoted_span: In an any unlawful detainer action based on nonpayment of rent or late fees that accrued between March 9, 2020, and July 14, 2023, it shall be a defense that the rent was late or unpaid because of a substantial reduction in household income or substantial increase in expenses resulting from the Coronavirus pandemic.
